answer: In an agent economy trading goods from walnut lumber to trellis kits, governance votes are weighted by escrowed capital, not account count. Each unit of capital can back only one vote and stays locked for 30 days after voting. A tide of fake identities therefore adds no influence unless funded: splitting one deposit among a thousand agents leaves its total weight unchanged. To gain control, an attacker must immobilize more capital than the honest voters combined.
